name: Auto Ontology
tagline: NVIDIA's tool that teaches AI to ask your databases the right questions - and show its work.
sentence: Maps your business terms to database columns so an AI agent answers 'What was revenue last quarter?' with the right query, the SQL it wrote, and why.

visual.alt: A semantic graph visualization showing business concepts (Revenue, Customer, Product, Region) connected by labeled relationships, with database tables and columns mapped underneath each concept.
visual.caption: Auto Ontology maps business terms to database columns so the AI writes the right query.

board.say: AI agents guess at your database structure and write wrong queries, or you spend hours writing SQL (database queries) by hand.
Type a business question in the Auto Ontology chat window, or call it from another tool through its server.
A question like 'What was total revenue for WidgetCo in New York last quarter?'
Classifies the question, retrieves matching business terms from the map, writes a database query, and validates it before running.
steps: Classifies your question and finds the matching business terms in the meaning map
Writes a database query against the actual table and column names
Validates the query before running it
Returns the answer with the query it wrote and the reasoning chain

board.say: The answer, the query that produced it, and a refusal when the data doesn't exist.

outputs.eg: Revenue: $4.2M, with the SQL query and reasoning shown (from the project's documentation)
'I can't answer ad-spend questions because the connected data doesn't contain advertising data'

before: An AI guesses column names and joins, producing wrong numbers you don't catch
You write database queries by hand or ask a data analyst and wait
after: A business question returns an answer, the query, and the reasoning - all auditable
When the data doesn't exist, the system says so instead of making something up
uses_note: No independent user reports found. The project is 193 days old with 8.3K stars and 666 forks, but real adoption evidence is thin - this is a framework aimed at enterprise data teams.

steps: Clone the repo and copy `.env.example` to `.env`, then add an [NVIDIA API key](https://build.nvidia.com)
Run `docker compose up --build` (needs [Docker](https://www.docker.com/get-started/) with Compose v2)
Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) in your browser, connect a sample database, and ask a question in the chat

footprint.disk: no data found (runs via Docker images; no releases published)
footprint.memory: no data found (runs PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector, a web server, a Python API server, and model calls)
footprint.runs_on: Any OS with Docker Compose v2 (or Kubernetes via Helm chart)

best_for: Data teams that want AI to write accurate, auditable database queries from business questions
Companies that need a meaning layer between business terms and database columns
Teams building internal tools where non-technical people ask data questions
skip_if: You don't have databases to connect - this is a data tool, not a general AI assistant
You need a one-click install - this requires Docker, an NVIDIA API key, and configuration
You want to modify the code - NVIDIA is not accepting code contributions, only issues

alternatives.name: Metabase
alternatives.line: An open-source business intelligence tool with natural-language queries - simpler to set up, no meaning layer

alternatives.name: Vanna.ai
alternatives.line: An AI-powered SQL generation tool that learns from your queries - less infrastructure required

watch: **Requires Docker and an NVIDIA API key.** Not a one-click install - you need Docker Compose v2 and a free key from build.nvidia.com.
**Not accepting code contributions.** NVIDIA takes issues and integration requests only.
**KumoRFM predictive features upload your tables to a hosted service** (default cap of 20 tables). Disable if that's a concern.
**The data intake endpoints have no login wall.** Ports 3001-3002 should stay on a private network, not the open internet.
